params.name: usagePathway

payload.latex:
\begin{aligned}
y_0 &= \operatorname{relu}\bigl( 0.521 x_{totalDayMinutes} \\
&\quad + 0.213 x_{totalNightMinutes_a} \\
&\quad - 1.01 x_{voiceMailPlan_b} \\
&\quad + 0.548 \operatorname{relu}{\left(0.66 x_{totalEveMinutes_a} + 1.2 \operatorname{relu}{\left(- 0.882 x_{state:41_b} + 0.537 x_{totalDayCharge} - 0.508 \right)} + 0.511 \right)} \\
&\quad -0.996 \bigr)
\end{aligned}

params.hypothesis:
Total-usage score. 1406=relu(0.537*dayCharge-0.882*state41-0.508); 7558=relu(0.511+0.660*eveMinutes+1.204*1406); 879=relu(-0.996+0.548*7558+0.521*dayMinutes+0.213*nightMinutes-1.011*voiceMailPlan). A hinge on a weighted sum of day (charge and minutes, identical after z-scoring), evening and night usage, lowered by having a voicemail plan; zero for ~2/3 of customers (light/average users).

Evidence (train, n=4000): 879 is a single hinge on a usage score. Pre-activation = -0.996 + 0.521*dayMinutes + 0.213*nightMinutes - 1.011*voiceMailPlan + 0.548*relu(0.511 + 0.660*eveMinutes + 1.204*relu(-0.508 + 0.537*dayCharge - 0.882*state41)). dayCharge and dayMinutes are the same column after z-scoring (max diff 5e-4), so day usage enters twice (directly and via 1406); eve and night likewise equal their charge columns. 879 is active in 34% of train rows: 1% of the lowest day-minute decile, 78% of the top decile. Voicemail-plan customers (1,061 rows): 879 is NEVER active (0/1061), so the whole usage risk is switched off for them; it is active in 46% of non-voicemail rows. State 41 (66 rows) forces 1406 off (0/66), removing the day-charge feed for those rows. Linear R2 of 879 on its inputs: 0.53. Sensitivity (train, n=4000): voiceMailPlan 0.34, dayMinutes 0.18, eveMinutes 0.11, state41 0.08, nightMinutes 0.07, dayCharge 0.05.

params.name: usageResponse
params.hypothesis:
How the usage score 879 (child usagePathway) becomes logit: identity_usage = 2.566*u + 2.868*relu(-0.384+0.750*customerServiceCalls-3.234*u) + 3.049*relu(-0.638+1.164*relu(-0.158+1.069*u)), u=879. Three parts: a direct linear slope on u; a service-calls gate (4344) that only lets customer service calls raise churn while u is near zero; and a delayed second hinge (14351->10552) that makes the response convex for the heaviest users.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Logit term = 2.566*u + 3.049*relu(-0.638+1.164*relu(-0.158+1.069u)) + 2.868*relu(-0.384+0.750*CSC-3.234u), u=879. (1) Usage: mean usage term by day-minute decile 0.01,0.01,0.05,0.14,0.17,0.28,0.44,0.68,1.20,3.94; the second hinge 10552 is on in 64% of the top decile, making the response convex; top-decile train churn 0.49 vs 0.06-0.17 elsewhere. (2) Service-calls gate 4344: closed for 0-2 calls (0% on), opens from 3 calls (68% on, mean term +0.81), 4 calls +2.12, 5 +3.61, 6 +5.32. Train churn by calls 0.115,0.110,0.110,0.106,0.437,0.571,0.679: the threshold is at 4 calls, and at 3 calls the gate already adds +0.8 logit that the data do not support (churn 0.106). The gate is shut by usage (-3.23u): at 4+ calls churn is 0.56-0.77 when u=0 but 0.20-0.38 when u>0. Logit sd 1.92; linear R2 of the term only 0.43. Train AUC 0.919; replacing this term by its least-squares linear fit in its 7 raw inputs gives 0.834 (all the gain over linear); mean-ablating it gives 0.655. Sub-parts restored alone onto the fully linearised model: usage hinge 879 slope +0.048, gate +0.038, second hinge +0.053 AUC.

params.name: intlPlanSwitch
params.hypothesis:
6711=relu(-0.230+0.633*internationalPlan), read out at 1.671. internationalPlan is binary, so this is an exact two-level offset: 0 for no plan, about +2.8 logit for international-plan customers.

Evidence (train, n=4000): internationalPlan is binary (z -0.324 / 3.086, 380 rows with plan). 6711 is off without the plan and 1.723 with it: +2.88 logit for plan holders (train churn 0.424 vs 0.112). Exactly linear (R2 1.0); mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.919 -> 0.862. No interaction with intl minutes/calls: those enter only linearly in linearBackbone.

params.name: voicemailState41Offset
params.hypothesis:
582=relu(1.517+0.093*state41+0.164*voiceMailPlan) is positive for every training row, so it is an exact affine term: a constant plus small negative offsets (readout -1.406) for voicemail-plan and state-41 rows.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Pre-activation min 1.406 on train, so 582 is always on: exactly affine. Logit term = -1.406*582: -0.23 for voicemail-plan rows and -1.03 for state 41 rows relative to others. Mean-ablation changes train AUC by -0.0007.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Pre-activation min 1.406 on train, so 582 is always on: exactly affine. Logit term = -1.406*582: -0.52 logit for voicemail-plan rows (1,061) and -1.03 for state 41 rows (66) relative to others. Mean-ablation changes train AUC by -0.0007.

params.hypothesis:
Per-state logit offsets: 19 direct state one-hot edges plus six single-input relu units (5821 state0, 2067 state45, 12726 state15, 13164 state41, 13420 state49, 5667 state2 which is dead). Every unit sees one binary one-hot, so the whole block is an exact sum of per-state offsets (a lookup table over states), not an interaction.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Exact per-state lookup (linear R2 1.0). Largest offsets (logit, total effect of the one-hot incl. other paths; rows; warranted offset logit(obs churn)-logit(model mean pred without the offset)): state46 -1.88 (80 rows, 5 churn; warranted -0.81); state39 -1.23 (82, 5; -0.60); state47 +1.09 (72, 21; +0.44); state5 -1.09 (78, 7; -0.43); state45 -0.97 (91, 6; -0.42, mostly via hidden 2067); state26 +0.81 (75, 16; +0.43); state49 -0.69 (122, 13; -0.15, via 13420); state0 -0.68 (56, 4; -0.25, via 5821); state10 -0.63 (60, 7; -0.18). Every large offset is about twice the size the data warrant: classic rare-category overfitting. 5667 (state2) is dead (never active). 12726 (state15) is always on, affine. Mean-ablation drops train AUC 0.919 -> 0.912.

payload.method: local forward passes; child replaced by least-squares linear fit on its raw input columns

params.hypothesis:
Root: logit = -1.959 + usageResponse + 1.671*intlPlanSwitch - 1.406*voicemailState41Offset + stateOffsets + linearBackbone, output sigmoid. Purely additive combination of five children; the only nonlinearity (and all of the AUC gain over a linear model) is inside usageResponse: a usage hinge that is shut for voicemail-plan customers, a customer-service-calls gate that opens at 3+ calls only for light users, and a convex second hinge for the heaviest users. The 35 unconnected inputs (states, areaCode 408/415, day/eve calls, eve/night charge, intl minutes) are zero-effect entries.

Evidence (train, n=4000): Train AUC 0.919. Replacing every child by its least-squares linear fit gives 0.834 (a refit L2 LR on all 71 inputs: 0.843). The whole +0.085 gain comes from usageResponse (restoring it alone onto the linearised model: +0.085; the other four children are exactly linear, R2 1.0, gain 0). Inside usageResponse, linearising the direct usage slope, the service-calls gate or the second usage hinge alone costs 0.010, 0.020 and 0.011 AUC. Mean-ablation: usageResponse 0.655, intlPlanSwitch 0.862, stateOffsets 0.912, linearBackbone 0.915, voicemailState41Offset 0.919. Rare-category offsets are linear but oversized: state46 -1.88 logit on 80 rows (warranted -0.81), state39 -1.23 (-0.60), state47 +1.09 (+0.44), state5 -1.09 (-0.43), state45 -0.97 (-0.42), state26 +0.81 (+0.43), state49 -0.69 (-0.15), state0 -0.68 (-0.25), state10 -0.63 (-0.18).
